cards.text: This is a psalm of David, the shepherd who became king of Israel (1 Samuel 16:11-13; 2 Samuel 5:3), written for the choirmaster. David doesn't ease into it, friend. He opens with praise: "O LORD, our Lord, how majestic is Your name in all the earth!"

cards.question: David says God's name is majestic in all the earth. Where does he say God has set His glory?

cards.text: Then David talks about praise that God Himself has ordained. And wait till you hear whose voices He picks for it.

cards.question: From whose mouths does David say God has ordained praise?
David says God ordained praise from children and infants on account of His adversaries, to ___ the enemy and avenger.

cards.text: Then David looks up at the heavens, the work of God's fingers, the moon and the stars He set in place. I do that over my bakery some nights, friend, and I just STAND there with my mouth open until the oven timer starts yelling at me.

cards.question: Looking up at all that sky, David asks God a question. Which one does he ask?

answers.text: What is man that You care for him
Why do the wicked prosper on the earth
How long will You hide Your face from me

cards.text: Next David compares man to the angels. For something so small under that giant sky, man ends up surprisingly close to them.

cards.question: True or false: David says God made man a little lower than the angels.

cards.text: Then David says God crowned man with glory and honor. A CROWN, friend, and the last thing anybody crowned ME with was dust in the back of a junk drawer!

cards.question: David says God made man ___ of the works of His hands.
David says God placed everything under man's feet. True or false: David's list stops with the animals that live on land.

cards.text: Here's David's whole list of what God put under man's feet: sheep and oxen, the beasts of the field, the birds of the air, and the fish of the sea, all that swim the paths of the seas. Meanwhile, the only thing under MY feet is this gold base!
And David ends right where he started: "O LORD, our Lord, how majestic is Your name in all the earth!" Friend, I need a minute. Somebody hand me an apron to cry into.
